article.title: How to Propose to an Ex-Girlfriend Again After a Breakup
article.excerpt: Whether you should propose to an ex-girlfriend again turns almost entirely on who ended it. Three situations, five signs the door is genuinely open, four cases where reaching out is wrong, and the honest case for sending nothing at all.
article.metaTitle: How to Propose to an Ex-Girlfriend Again — And When Not To
article.metaDescription: How to propose to an ex-girlfriend again turns on who ended it. In a study of 387 people, those whose partner ended it carried more grief. Three cases.
article.keywords: how to propose ex girlfriend again, propose to ex girlfriend, asking an ex to marry you, getting back together after a breakup, should i contact my ex
keyTakeaways: Whether reaching out is reasonable turns on who ended it: in a 2020 study of 387 people aged 18-40, those whose partner ended the relationship reported higher breakup grief (M = 2.88) than those who ended it themselves (M = 2.36).

Four cases make contact wrong outright — she asked for space, she is with someone else, the relationship involved coercion or abuse, or contact would be unwelcome. Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 makes repeated contact despite a clear indication of disinterest the offence of stalking, punishable by up to three years on a first conviction.

The urgency is a documented phase, not a signal: across 14 biweekly waves with 69 students, self-concept clarity dropped immediately at the breakup wave (B = -0.44, p < .05), and among 312 people who had broken up, distress predicted obsessive pursuit of the ex-partner.
If there is something to apologise for it comes first and separately — the apology page is the most-built page type on SubhSandesh, 1,347 of 5,061 pages, 26.6% platform-wide across 20 page types.
For many readers the right answer is no page, no message and no gesture at all, and this post says so in its own section.

faqs.question: Is it ever okay to propose to an ex-girlfriend?
faqs.answer: Only when the relationship has genuinely restarted and she has shown she wants it, which is rare and slow. If she ended it and has not been in touch, a proposal is a question she has already answered. A proposal is not a way to reopen a relationship; it is something you do inside one.

faqs.question: How do I know if my ex-girlfriend wants me back?
faqs.answer: You look for things she does without being prompted: contacting you first on separate occasions, referring to a future with you in it, and talking to you directly rather than through friends. None of these can be engineered, which is exactly why they mean something. If you have to look hard for a sign, that is your answer.

faqs.question: She ended it and has not messaged me. Should I reach out?
faqs.answer: No. Her decision is information, not an obstacle to work around. In a 2020 study of 387 people, those whose partner ended the relationship carried more grief than those who ended it themselves, so the silence you are reading as ambiguity is more likely her recovering.

faqs.question: Does the no contact rule work for getting an ex back?
faqs.answer: Treating silence as a tactic to make someone miss you is manipulation with a friendly name, and this page will not coach it. Not contacting someone who has not invited contact is simply the correct behaviour, not a move in a game. If you are counting the days until you are allowed to message, you are still pursuing.

faqs.question: How long should I wait before contacting my ex-girlfriend?
faqs.answer: There is no number, and any page that gives you one is guessing. The question is not how much time has passed but whether she has indicated she wants contact. If she has not, more waiting does not convert into permission.

faqs.question: What if she asked me for space?
faqs.answer: Then the answer is already given and nothing further should be sent, including a message explaining that you are respecting it. A boundary does not expire because weeks went by. This is the one signal that closes the door on its own, whatever else looks encouraging.

faqs.question: What if my ex-girlfriend has a new boyfriend?
faqs.answer: Do not contact her. Whatever you think of him is not relevant to whether contacting her is fair, and reaching out now puts her in the position of managing you on top of everything else. This is one of the four cases where reaching out is simply wrong.

faqs.question: Can repeatedly messaging an ex get me into legal trouble in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 makes it stalking for a man to contact or attempt to contact a woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest, punishable with imprisonment of up to three years on a first conviction and up to five years on a subsequent one. Monitoring her internet or messaging use is covered by the same section.

faqs.question: Should I apologise before I ask her anything?
faqs.answer: If there is genuinely something to apologise for, yes, and it should be its own message with no ask attached to it. An apology page is the most-built page type on SubhSandesh at 1,347 of 5,061 pages, 26.6% platform-wide across all 20 page types. A proposal sent into an unresolved ending makes the ending worse.

faqs.question: I was the one who ended it. Is it wrong to want her back?
faqs.answer: Wanting it is not wrong; acting on it without acknowledging what you did is. You removed something from her life, so the first thing you owe her is an account of that, not a question. She is also under no obligation to be available because you have changed your mind.

faqs.question: Why do I feel like I have to do something right now?
faqs.answer: Because that urgency is a documented feature of the weeks after a breakup rather than information about the relationship. In a six-month study, self-concept clarity dropped immediately when a breakup happened, and separate research on 312 people found that distress predicted obsessive pursuit of an ex-partner. The feeling is evidence about you.

faqs.question: Can a beautifully made page change her mind?
faqs.answer: No, and any page that suggests otherwise is selling you something. A page is a container; if what goes into it is pressure, making the container beautiful makes the pressure worse. For a large share of people reading this, the right output is no page at all.

article.contentMarkdown:
# How to Propose to an Ex-Girlfriend Again After a Breakup

Usually you should not, and whether you should at all turns on one thing: who ended it. If she ended the relationship and has not been in touch since, a proposal is not a romantic gesture — it is a question she has already answered.

The internet sells a technique for this. There is no technique, and this page does not contain one. What it contains is a way to read whether the door is genuinely open, the cases where contact is wrong, and permission to stop.

If something needs apologising for, that comes first and separately: the apology page is the most-built thing on SubhSandesh, 1,347 of the 5,061 personalised pages created since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types — 26.6% of everything built platform-wide.

## What asking again means once the relationship has actually ended

Proposing to an ex-girlfriend again means asking someone to marry you after the relationship between you has stopped existing. That is a different question from proposing after a row: a fight happens inside a relationship that is still running, while a breakup is the relationship's own answer to itself. If you are in the first case, the companion piece on [proposing again after a fight](/blog/how-to-propose-girlfriend-again-after-a-fight) is yours.

Three situations hide inside the same search, and they are not interchangeable.

**She ended it.** Her decision is information. It is not an obstacle, a negotiating position, or a test of how much you want it.

**You ended it.** You removed something from her life. What you owe her first is an account of that, not a question.

**It was mutual.** The only one where opening a conversation is reasonable — and even then it is a conversation, not a proposal.

Research on breakup grief supports the split. In a 2020 study of 387 people aged 18 to 40, those whose partners had more often ended the relationship reported higher grief (M = 2.88) than those who had more often ended it themselves (M = 2.36), t(365) = 4.62, p < .01, with initiator status still an independent predictor in a model explaining 28% of the variance. Work out which of you that is before assuming your pain is shared.

## Five signs the door is actually open

None can be manufactured, which is the point: a signal you engineered tells you nothing. Each gives what it is, what it is not, why it counts, and what to do.

### 1. She contacts you first, more than once, about nothing

**What it is:** she messages you unprompted, on separate occasions, with no practical reason — no returned charger, no booking.

**What it is not:** replying politely to you. A reply is manners.

**Why it counts:** initiating repeatedly costs her something, and she chooses to pay it.

**What to do:** answer warmly, at her pace, and do not escalate. Let three or four happen first.

### 2. She refers to a future that has you in it

**What it is:** an unprompted "we should go there sometime", or a plan assuming you are around in six months.

**What it is not:** nostalgia. Missing something is not wanting it back.

**Why it counts:** future talk is the cheapest thing to withhold and the hardest to fake accidentally.

**What to do:** nothing immediately. Note it, and see whether it happens twice.

### 3. The reason she gave was specific, and it has genuinely changed

**What it is:** she named a concrete problem — a city, a job, a behaviour — and it is now demonstrably different.

**What it is not:** you feeling you have changed. Self-reported change is not evidence.

**Why it counts:** a named, solved reason removes the obstacle instead of obscuring it.

**What to do:** let the change stand for months before mentioning it, and never present it as an invoice.

### 4. She is not asking you to go through other people

**What it is:** she talks to you directly when she talks to you at all.

**What it is not:** friends relaying that she "still asks about you". Using friends as a channel is pressure in disguise.

**Why it counts:** direct contact is the only contact she controls.

**What to do:** stop asking mutual friends anything, today.

### 5. She has never asked you for space

**What it is:** no request for distance, no block, no "please don't message me".

**What it is not:** a request she made once and has not repeated. A boundary does not expire because time passed.

**Why it counts:** this is the only item that closes the door on its own, whatever the other four say.

**What to do:** if she has asked, the answer is given. Honour it without a farewell message.

## What each of the three situations actually calls for

This sets the situations against what is reasonable now and how often each page type is built. The SubhSandesh figures are platform-wide across all 20 page types, never proposal-specific — no proposal-specific data exists.

| Situation | Is contact reasonable now? | What comes first | Page to build, if any (share of all 5,061 pages, platform-wide) |
|---|---|---|---|
| She ended it, no contact since | No | Nothing | None |
| She ended it, but has initiated contact more than once | Possibly, slowly | An apology, if owed | Apology page — 1,347 pages, 26.6% |
| You ended it, and she has not said she wants you back | No | An account of what you did | Apology page — 1,347 pages, 26.6% |
| Mutual ending, and you are both already talking | Yes, as a conversation | An invitation to meet | Invitation page |
| She has asked for space, or is seeing someone else | No | Nothing | None |

Three of five rows resolve to "nothing". That is the honest shape of this question.

## When reaching out is the wrong thing to do

Four cases, none with an exception you are the exception to.

**She has asked for space.** That is a complete answer. A message saying you are respecting it is still a message.

**She is seeing someone else.** What you think of him is irrelevant. Contacting her now makes her manage you.

**There was coercion, control, threat or violence, in either direction.** Reconciliation here is not romantic, it is risky. The 2025 validation study behind the Attitude Toward Returning to an Ex-Partner Scale, built with 55 women who had been victims of gender violence, says it plainly in its abstract: when a relationship ends because of abuse, a favourable attitude toward reconciliation can itself be a risk factor. Here the next step is a professional, not a page.

**Contact would be unwelcome and you already know it.** You usually do.

There is a legal line too, closer than most people assume. Under [section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023](https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2023/The%20Bharatiya%20Nyaya%20Sanhita,%202023.pdf), a man who contacts or attempts to contact a woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly, despite a clear indication of disinterest, commits the offence of stalking — punishable on a first conviction with imprisonment of up to three years and a fine, and up to five years on a subsequent conviction.

## Why the urgency feels like proof, and is not

The feeling that you must act now is a documented feature of the weeks after a breakup, not a message about the relationship.

In a six-month longitudinal study published in 2010, [69 undergraduates were assessed every two weeks across 14 waves](https://faculty.wcas.northwestern.edu/eli-finkel/documents/2010_SlotterGardnerFinkel_PSPB.pdf) and 26 broke up mid-study. Self-concept clarity — how clearly a person can say who they are — dropped immediately at the wave the breakup was reported (B = −0.44, p < .05), and the gradual rise the rest of the sample enjoyed flattened afterwards. Reduced clarity uniquely predicted how distressed people were.

The same research line connects that distress to the urge to pursue. Among [312 people who had broken up in the previous twelve months](https://ubwp.buffalo.edu/selfandmotivationlab/wp-content/uploads/sites/91/2018/05/Park-Sanchez-Bryndilsen-2011-JASP-1.pdf), the more strongly someone based their self-worth on being in a relationship, the more emotional distress they reported and the more obsessive pursuit of the ex-partner they engaged in — with distress partially mediating the link. The pursuit was a symptom of the pain, not a reading of the odds.

The urgency is evidence about you. It is not evidence about her.

## If the door is open, the order that respects her

**Apologise first, and separately.** If there is genuinely something to apologise for, it gets its own message, with no ask attached and no proposal near it. That is what the [apology page](/apology-dashboard) is for, and it is the most-built page type on the platform at 1,347 of 5,061, 26.6% platform-wide. A proposal sent into an unresolved ending makes the ending worse, because it asks her to skip the part she is still holding.

**Then ask for one conversation, not a life.** An [invitation page](/date-invitation) asking for a coffee she can decline in one tap is the right size of ask here. If the answer is no, that is the answer.

**Only much later, if you are actually back together, a proposal.** A [proposal scrapbook](/proposal) works when the relationship it describes currently exists. Write it slowly: the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours, sampled on the apology dashboard across 1,348 pages. Platform-wide, 38.7% of creators password-protect a page before sharing (1,961 of 5,061).

## When no page at all is the right answer

For many people who searched this, the correct output is nothing, and SubhSandesh is the wrong tool tonight. None of the 20 page types here, and no scrapbook of your story, changes a decision she made. A page is a container, and if what goes in it is pressure, a beautiful container makes the pressure worse.

It is also wrong when she has asked for space, when she has a new partner, when the ending involved coercion, or when you are building it mainly to feel better tonight. In that last case the honest move is to close the tab. She ended it, that is information, and accepting it is the only step here entirely within your control.

## Sources

- Slotter, Gardner & Finkel (2010). [Who Am I Without You? Romantic Breakup and the Self-Concept](https://faculty.wcas.northwestern.edu/eli-finkel/documents/2010_SlotterGardnerFinkel_PSPB.pdf). *Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin*, 36(2).
- Ranđelović & Goljović (2020). [Breakup Grief — Initiator and Non-Initiator](https://scindeks-clanci.ceon.rs/data/pdf/0354-3293/2020/0354-32932003047R.pdf). *Zbornik Radova Filozofskog Fakulteta u Prištini*, 50(3).
- Park, Sanchez & Brynildsen (2011). [Maladaptive Responses to Relationship Dissolution](https://ubwp.buffalo.edu/selfandmotivationlab/wp-content/uploads/sites/91/2018/05/Park-Sanchez-Bryndilsen-2011-JASP-1.pdf). *Journal of Applied Social Psychology*, 41(7).
- Vázquez et al. (2025). [Attitude Toward Returning to an Ex-Partner Scale](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-0760/14/9/528). *Social Sciences*, 14(9), 528. Abstract only.
- [Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, section 78](https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2023/The%20Bharatiya%20Nyaya%20Sanhita,%202023.pdf), Act No. 45 of 2023.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this because it is the only page in the set that answers the question with a rule rather than a technique: who ended it decides whether contact is reasonable, and that rule is backed by initiator-status, self-concept-clarity and distress-driven-pursuit research none of the surfaced results touch, plus the section 78 line on repeated contact after a clear indication of disinterest. It is also the only one that names four cases where reaching out is wrong and states that no page at all is the right answer for many readers. On traffic: this keyword sits in an under-300 EST band, so the page is not a traffic asset and should not be judged as one. A page at this volume exists to be the correct answer when the question is asked - by a person in a bad week, or by an assistant summarising this query - and to hold the ethical floor for the propose cluster that the higher-volume pages link into. Expect single-digit monthly sessions and measure it on whether it gets cited and whether it stops one person from doing something they cannot take back. It will not outrank the coaching funnels on commercial intent, because it refuses the thing they sell.
